item.title: Draft ministerial evaluation of digital platform transparency and fairness
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry published its draft 2026 ministerial evaluation under the Act on Improving Transparency and Fairness of Specified Digital Platforms for public comment on 2026-11-20; the stated deadline is 2026-12-20 13:00 JST. Covering general merchandise online malls and digital advertising, the draft identifies concerns about impersonation advertisements, account suspension explanations, advertising auction fee disclosures, complaint handling, and coordination with overseas operations. Platform-specific findings address Google, Meta, LINE Yahoo, TikTok, Amazon and Rakuten, including Amazon's use of reported information to address misconduct and its return/refund decisions, and Rakuten's paid seller services. The draft requests that responses to its principal findings be described in periodic reports; it is a proposed evaluation, not a new or amending legislative instrument. item.title: Draft ministerial ordinance and notices on maritime radio stations and equipment
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications announced a public consultation on 2026-11-20 on a draft ministerial ordinance amending the Fundamental Standards for Establishing Radio Stations (excluding basic broadcasting stations) and related rules. The draft Article 5 would expand permitted communication counterparts for fisheries coast stations to include radio stations aboard non-fishing vessels, while retaining a condition that communications concern the specified persons' fishing activities and be minimal. The package would amend seven ordinances, the Frequency Assignment Plan and related notices, and introduce a new notice establishing technical conditions for autonomous maritime radio equipment. Other listed subjects include ship and aircraft station frequency symbols, distress-alert station equipment testing, ship earth stations and digital selective calling equipment for ship and coast stations. The excerpts do not establish a comment deadline, commencement date or the detailed technical changes across the full package. item.title: Draft Cabinet Order aligning mobile subscriber verification and misuse-prevention rules
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications announced this draft Cabinet Order consultation on 2026-11-19, with a stated consultation period of 2026-11-20 to 2026-12-21 and a listed deadline of 2026-12-21 23:59 JST. The draft supports Act No. 25 of 2026, promulgated on 2026-05-29, which amends the Act on Identification of Subscribers by Mobile Voice Communications Operators and Prevention of Improper Use of Mobile Voice Communications Services (Act No. 31 of 2005), including extending identity verification at contract conclusion to mobile data communications services. It would amend Cabinet Order No. 171 of 2005 to reflect the renamed Act and expand the offenses specified under Article 8(1)(ii), including specified unauthorized computer access and criminal-proceeds transfer offenses. It would also update references in Cabinet Order No. 146 of 2005 concerning laws covered by whistleblower protection and Cabinet Order No. 180 of 1954 concerning the National Police Agency's organization. The draft specifies commencement on 2027-04-01, alongside the amending Act; it is not presented as a finalized Cabinet Order. item.title: Draft ordinance and notice amendments on mobile-service incentives and MVNO regulation
item.description: AI summary: The proposed Ministerial Ordinance would relax restrictions on benefits conditional on new mobile-service contracts, allowing installment-based provision of communication-fee discounts and other benefits within a JPY 20,000 ceiling. It would also subject mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs) to the relevant rules when their contract share for regulated services exceeds 4%, regardless of affiliation with a mobile network operator (MNO); the proposed Notice would remove designations of MNO-affiliated MVNOs. The package would amend the Regulations for Enforcement of the Telecommunications Business Act and Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications Notice No. 291 of 2023, under the Telecommunications Business Act (Act No. 86 of 1984). The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications consultation was announced in a document dated 2026-11-18 and listed on 2026-11-19, with a stated comment deadline of 2026-12-18 at 23:59 JST; postal submissions may bear the deadline date's postmark. The excerpts do not establish an effective date. item.description: AI summary: The Digital Agency published an advance notice on 2026-11-13 announcing planned CSV format changes for town and aza subdivision data in the Address Base Registry, alongside a system renewal in late January 2027. Residential-address, residential-block and land-parcel-number data may also change. Temporary access to the existing format for existing users is under consideration, but data added or updated after the renewal is planned to be available only in the new format. The notice states that ABR Geocoder users will need a new version; changes to its API definitions may also require adjustments to systems using it. Detailed changes, sample CSV data and the system renewal date are scheduled to be announced around December 2026. item.title: FSA publishes study-group discussion summary on digital and decentralized finance
item.description: AI summary: The Financial Services Agency published a summary on 2026-11-12 of the first meeting in administrative year 2026 of its Study Group on Approaches to Digital and Decentralized Finance. Following hearings with Nomura Holdings, Inc. and Securitize Japan Co., Ltd., participants discussed on-chain finance, tokenized payment instruments and assets, and possible regulatory approaches, rather than adopted rule changes. Opinions addressed anti-money-laundering risks, financial institutions' custody and return of assets, system audit disclosures, incident controls, settlement finality and regulation of AI use. Participants also raised tokenized-deposit interoperability and questioned whether existing regulation sufficiently addresses large redemptions by major electronic payment instrument issuers and lending combined with issuance.
